title: Stalk calculation for a map with the closed-structure tensor section formula
statement: Let i:Z→Y be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let M be an O_Y-module sheaf, and set B=i_*O_Z. Let α:M tensor B→i_*i^*M be a module map, using the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Assume that for each open U of Y, section s of M on U and section r of O_Z on i⁻¹U, α(s tensor r)=r times η_M(s), where η is the canonical tensor-pullback/pushforward adjunction unit [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Then the map induced by α on the underlying abelian-group stalk at any point x of Y is an isomorphism. No naturality in M is assumed, and no map is constructed by this assertion.

proof.text: Identify the stalk of the unit module with the stalk ring using the filtered-colimit comparison for the composite forgetful functor CommRingCat to RingCat to AddCommGrpCat. The comparison carries each unit-module germ to the corresponding ring germ. To prove linearity, represent the scalar and vector on a common open neighbourhood and apply preservation of multiplication by the ring germ map. This is the fully proved private helper projection_unit_stalk_iso, following the existing private calculation in ClosedImmersionUnitStalkKernel.

For x=i(z), take the stalk-tensor isomorphism Phi, the tensor-pullback stalk isomorphism delta, and closed-pushforward stalk maps for B=i_*O_Z and P=i^*M. Composing the B comparison with the unit-stalk comparison gives an additive equivalence b:B_x to O_Z,z. Its semilinearity makes b an O_Y,x-linear equivalence beta to the scalar-restricted ring. Tensor beta with the identity of M_x and compose with tensor symmetry to obtain an additive equivalence q:M_x tensor B_x to O_Z,z tensor M_x. Compose the P comparison with delta to obtain the target additive equivalence epsilon. On a germ of s tensor r, the assumed section formula, the pushforward germ formula, the stalk scalar formula, and the pullback-unit germ formula give epsilon(alpha_x(germ(s tensor r)))=q(germ(s) tensor germ(r)). For arbitrary pure stalk tensors, represent both entries by sections on Y and restrict to the intersection of their neighbourhoods. Phi sends the corresponding pure tensor section germ to the pure stalk tensor. Additive tensor induction therefore shows epsilon composed with alpha_x composed with Phi inverse equals q. Injectivity and surjectivity follow by cancellation and lifting through these equivalences; the concrete-category criterion gives IsIso.

For x outside the closed image, the closed-pushforward stalk theorem makes both B_x and (i_*P)_x subsingleton. The tensor of M_x with B_x is subsingleton, and the stalk-tensor equivalence transports this to (M tensor B)_x. The given stalk morphism is injective because its source is subsingleton and surjective because its target is subsingleton and its source contains zero. The concrete-category bijectivity criterion proves IsIso.

theorem closedStructure_projection_stalk_isIso
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i] (M : Y.Modules)
    (α : M ⊗ (pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf) ⟶
      (pushforward i).obj ((tensorPullback i).obj M))
    (hα : ∀ (U : Y.Opens) (s : Γ(M, U))
      (r : Γ((pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf), U)),
      α.app U (tmulSection s r) = (show Γ(Z, i ⁻¹ᵁ U) from r) •
        (show Γ((tensorPullback i).obj M, i ⁻¹ᵁ U) from
          ((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction i)).unit.app M).app U s))
    (x : Y) :
    IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x).map α.mapPresheaf)
